newsitem.title: UGANDA: Zaire rebel backers seize embassy in Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel backers seize embassy in Uganda.

text.p: Supporters of Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila seized Zaire's embassy in Uganda on Monday but were forced out by police, diplomatic and police sources said on Tuesday.

Police sources said a group of 50 Zaireans living in Uganda stormed the embassy, set ablaze Zaire's flag, broke a portrait of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and demanded embassy staff pledge loyalty to Kabila.
No injuries were reported during the 40-minute takeover.
The group overpowered embassy security men before forcing their way in. They then hoisted the flag of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).
The state-owned New Vision newspaper quoted Walumba Mbuliyenda, chairman of the Zairean community in Uganda, as saying that his group was monitoring events at the embassy.
"We have not been violent because we are supporters of democracy and cherish peace," it quoted Mbuliyenda as saying.
The foreign ministry described the seizure of the embassy as criminal and urged police to charge those involved.
"That is criminal trespass and those people should be charged," said foreign ministry spokesman Louis Balinda.
Ugandan police were stationed outside the embassy on Tuesday.
The rebels have seized about one quarter of Zaire since October last year.
